sources.title: The Impact of Conflict, Climate and the Economy on Agriculture in Districts of Return in Iraq
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration and Social Inquiry
geographic_coverage: 14 districts of return across Anbar, Diyala, Kirkuk, Ninewa and Salah al-Din
sources.temporal_coverage: Household data collected March-April 2022; report published 2024
sources.methodology: Survey of 2,260 returnees in 14 districts, collected March-April 2022.
sources.limitations: Self-reported and limited to sampled return districts.

sources.title: Cracked Earth, shrinking harvest: Drought impact on displaced and returnee Iraqis
sources.temporal_coverage: Displacement and returnee conditions, with 2023-2024 drought indicators
sources.methodology: Publisher page summarizes drought and displacement survey findings in named governorates.
sources.limitations: Full report methods were unavailable in the inspected excerpt.

sources.title: Applying causality to environmental security in Iraq
sources.temporal_coverage: Subdistrict observations from January 2020 to January 2022
sources.methodology: Observational subdistrict analysis using structural equation modeling and causal-inference methods with conflict and environmental indicators.
sources.limitations: Authors note omitted social and political variables, limited temporal coverage and mismatches between tribal and administrative boundaries.

sources.title: Context and Conflict Analysis: Sustainable and Resilient Future Ninewa Project
sources.organization: World Vision International / Australian NGO Cooperation Program
sources.methodology: Participatory qualitative assessment using eight focus groups and ten key-informant interviews across four Ninewa areas.
sources.limitations: Purposive qualitative sample is not statistically representative; findings describe participants' reported conditions and views.

claims.locator: PDF p. 3, farming and livestock production findings
claims.paraphrase: Nearly 75% of surveyed farming households reported lower harvests than in 2014; over 80% of livestock owners reported smaller herds.
geographies: 14 districts of return: Mosul, Ramadi, Falluja, Telafar, Tikrit, Heet, Hawija, Hamdaniya, Shirqat, Kirkuk, Baiji, Sinjar, Khanaqin and Balad

claims.locator: PDF pp. 2 and 4, conflict and agricultural recovery
claims.paraphrase: ISIL-era conflict destroyed farm assets and infrastructure; limited replacement capacity and incentives hindered agricultural recovery.
geographies: Districts of return in Anbar, Diyala, Kirkuk, Ninewa and Salah al-Din
claims.limitations: Multiple barriers; relative effects not isolated.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Conflict destruction and limited asset replacement hindered post-conflict agricultural recovery.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 4 and 6, reasons for reduced production and abandonment
claims.paraphrase: Respondents cited water scarcity and weather; lack of water explained about a quarter of farm abandonment and weather about a tenth.
geographies: Northern districts including Sinjar, Shirqat, Hamdaniya and Telafar
claims.limitations: Respondent attributions; economic and conflict factors also mattered.

claims.paraphrase: The report recommends early warning and technology investment to support agriculture and durable returns.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Unaddressed agricultural recovery could undermine reintegration and return durability.

claims.paraphrase: In the 2024 farming season, 57% of surveyed returnee households used less land or water; 5% reported being forced to move because of drought conditions.
claims.limitations: Publisher summary only; questionnaire, denominator and detailed methods were not available in the inspected page.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: NRC reports that drought conditions forced some returnee households to move and that many reduced land or water use.

claims.locator: Publisher summary, displaced households in informal sites
claims.paraphrase: Among displaced households in informal sites, one in five lacked clean water, three quarters reported water-sharing tensions, and 44% said authorities barred some groups from water.
claims.limitations: Publisher summary only; results are not disaggregated further in the accessible excerpt.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report summary explicitly connects drought-related water stress with tensions and differential access in displacement sites.

claims.paraphrase: The report says four in five displaced respondents linked return decisions to the ability to farm, and 93% based stay, move or return decisions on information about local resources.
geographies: Displacement sites in Anbar, Duhok, Ninewa and Salah al-Din
claims.limitations: Publisher summary only; do not interpret stated decision factors as observed return outcomes.

claims.locator: Abstract and results, environmental variables and battle events
claims.paraphrase: Across 294 subdistricts from 2020-2022, the study reports a direct association between skin temperature and battle events, with soil moisture and energy operating indirectly.
claims.limitations: Observational model; authors note omitted social and political variables and limited temporal specificity.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The authors report modeled direct and indirect relationships between environmental indicators and battle events; these are observational findings, not experimental proof.

claims.paraphrase: Population density positively mediated modeled conflict activity, while wheat production did not reduce conflict as hypothesized.
claims.limitations: Model result is limited by omitted social-political variables and the 2020-2022 period.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The authors' model identifies population density as a positive mediator and does not support the hypothesized wheat-production pathway.

claims.locator: PDF p. 10, climate and conflict findings for Nimrud and Hatra
claims.paraphrase: Participants described drought, reduced rainfall and water scarcity as undermining farming and increasing irrigation and land competition, including farmer-herder tension in rural Nimrud and Hatra.
claims.limitations: Qualitative perceptions from purposive February 2026 fieldwork; not a representative estimate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Participants describe climate stress as increasing competition over land and irrigation and as a conflict multiplier in the named rural areas.

claims.locator: PDF p. 10, access and inclusion findings
claims.paraphrase: Participants reported that women, youth, people with disabilities, low-income households and displaced or returnee groups face unequal access to land, capital, irrigation and employment in parts of Ninewa.
claims.limitations: Reported qualitative access barriers; the assessment does not estimate prevalence.

claims.locator: PDF p. 10, local capacities for peace
claims.paraphrase: The assessment identifies tribal mediation, kinship networks, shared economic activity and community initiatives as local peace capacities, while noting exclusion of less-connected groups.
claims.limitations: Qualitative assessment; capacities are described, not impact-evaluated.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The assessment identifies social mediation and shared economic activity as existing capacities for preventing or managing local conflict.

search_audit.query: Iraq governorate subnational climate vulnerability conflict water scarcity report 2025 primary source
search_audit.outcome: Found district-level returnee agriculture data and governorate-level drought/displacement findings; UNDP index full PDF was not accessible.

search_audit.query: Iraq climate conflict mediators armed groups grievances climate insecurity subnational original report 2025 2026
search_audit.outcome: Found Ninewa qualitative participant accounts of farmer-herder/land and irrigation tensions, and an observational subdistrict environmental-security study; no climate-only causal claim adopted.

search_audit.query: Iraq conflict to climate reverse link damage infrastructure climate adaptation governance report Mosul returnees
search_audit.outcome: IOM survey documents conflict destruction and limited agricultural asset replacement; this supports a conflict-to-recovery link, not an unsupported adaptation claim.

search_audit.query: Iraq local climate resilience peace capacity adaptation committees water governance primary evaluation governorate
search_audit.outcome: Found Ninewa mediation capacities and adaptation recommendations; no evaluated impact claim was found in these sources.

gaps: Recent local conflict-climate evidence is concentrated in Ninewa, selected return districts and displacement sites; findings are not nationally representative.
NRC detailed report methods were unavailable in the inspected excerpt, and the UNDP climate-vulnerability PDF could not be opened.
Evidence on tested climate-adaptation outcomes that reduce FCV risk remains limited in the inspected materials.
